ex.en: Office workers often suffer neck pain from staring at screens all day.
ex.zh: 办公室职员整天盯着屏幕，常常颈部疼痛。

ex.en: The necklace, a family heirloom, had been passed down for five generations.
ex.zh: 这条项链是传家宝，已经传了五代人。

books.unit: 常见冠词、情态动词、系动词与限定词

ex.en: There is a growing need for teachers trained in special education.
ex.zh: 对受过特殊教育培训的教师的需求日益增长。

ex.en: The compass needle points north because the Earth itself acts as a magnet.
ex.zh: 指南针的指针指向北方，因为地球本身就如同一块磁铁。

ex.en: Critics say the form is needlessly complex and discourages poorer families from applying.
ex.zh: 批评者说该表格不必要地复杂，令贫困家庭不敢申请。

ex.en: The audit highlighted the needlessness of keeping paper copies now that records are digital.
ex.zh: 审计指出，在记录已数字化的今天保留纸质副本没有必要。

ex.en: The scholarship is reserved for needy students from remote rural districts.
ex.zh: 该奖学金专门面向来自偏远农村地区的贫困学生。

ex.en: Parents who neglect to read to their children may widen the school-readiness gap.
ex.zh: 不给孩子读书的家长可能会扩大学业准备方面的差距。

senses: adj. 否定的，消极的；阴性的
adj. 消极的，负面的，否定的
adj. 负面的；【数】负的；否定的；阴性的
negative.usage: adj.否定的，拒绝的；有 害的，不良的；负面的， 消极的；adj.否定的；有害的；消极的； 阴性的；负的 n.底片；否定词，否定 v.否绝，拒绝；neg（否认，拒绝）+ative（有……倾向的）→否认的；否定的；词根:neg(deny否定)+ative(形容词后缀)→否定的；例为2020年新题型，跨前页；索引p412

ex.en: One study found that people responded best to comments that shifted from negative to positive.
ex.zh: 一项研究发现，人们对从消极转变为积极的评论反应最好。

ex.en: A more direct finding is that people who scored high for negative emotions like anxiety looked at others for shorter periods of time and reported more comfortable feelings when others did not look directly at them.
ex.zh: 另一个更为直接的发现是：比如焦虑等负面情绪方面得分高的人，注视别人的时间要更短，而且他们报告说在别人不直视他们时，他们会感觉更舒适。

ex.en: Constant exposure to negative news can harm people's mental well-being.
ex.zh: 持续接触负面新闻会损害人们的心理健康。

negatively.usage: adv.消极地；否定地 史密斯夫妇都不会想到他的spouse 是一个spy, 这让他（她）很annoyed，连腰belt 上都有窃听器。这一 点也不cool，elite 阶层的他们却要防止被hijack, 还要hire 保镖去处理latte

ex.en: The report warns that air pollution affects children's lungs negatively even at low levels.
ex.zh: 报告警告，即使浓度很低，空气污染也会对儿童肺部产生不利影响。

senses: n. 忽略；忽视；不予重视
v. 忽略；忽视；疏忽；不予重视；疏于照顾
neglect.usage: v.疏忽，忽略；漏做 n.忽略，忽视；发音类似“那个赖他”→因为他的“疏忽”导致事情没有做好，所以要赖他。；vt.不予重视例为2013年新题型；索引p412

ex.en: But the intention is not to neglect social science.
ex.zh: 但其目的并不是要忽视社会科学。

ex.en: But the intention is not to neglect social science; rather, the complete opposite.
ex.zh: 但（这一做法的）目的并不是要忽视社会科学，恰恰相反，是重视它。

ex.en: Years of neglect had left the historic building in a dangerous state.
ex.zh: 多年的疏于维护使这座历史建筑处于危险状态。

negligence.usage: n.疏忽，大意；玩忽职守；索引p412

ex.en: The hospital was sued for negligence after the patient's records were lost.
ex.zh: 病人的病历丢失后，这家医院因玩忽职守被起诉。

ex.en: The accident was caused by the negligence of the site manager.
ex.zh: 事故是由工地经理的疏忽造成的。

ex.en: Courts distinguish between honest error and gross negligence.
ex.zh: 法院会区分无心的过失和严重的疏忽。

senses: adj. 疏忽的，微不足道的
negligible.usage: adj.微不足道的，不值一提的

ex.en: The company says the cost of relocation will be negligible.
ex.zh: 公司说搬迁的费用微不足道。

ex.en: The difference in test scores between the two groups was statistically negligible.
ex.zh: 两组之间的考试成绩差异在统计上微不足道。

ex.en: Switching off unused lights saves a negligible amount of energy, so focus on heating instead.
ex.zh: 关掉不用的灯所节省的能源微乎其微，所以应把重点放在供暖上。

senses: vt. 通过谈判达成（或解决）
v. 谈判；磋商；协商；商定，达成（协议）
negotiate.usage: negotiate a contract 商定合同；[族] negotiation n. 谈判；磋商；[近] bargain vi. 谈判（链P312）；neg（不）+oti（闲暇）+-ate→商人没有闲暇→忙于谈判→协商。族negotiation n.谈判；negotiator n.谈判者；v.谈判，洽谈；商定，达成

ex.en: Either way, one benefit of a national organization would be to negotiate better prices.
ex.zh: 无论哪种方式，全国性组织的一个好处是可以协商更好的价格。

ex.en: Negotiated by USFWS and the states, the plan requires individuals and businesses that damage habitat as part of their operations to pay into a fund to replace every acre destroyed with 2 new acres of suitable habitat.
ex.zh: 经过美国鱼类及野生动植物管理局(USFWS)和各州协商，该计划要求那些因经营需要而破坏栖息地的个人和企业向一项基金缴纳费用，每有一英亩栖息地遭到破坏，就建造两英亩新的合适的栖息地。

ex.en: The union plans to negotiate with management over pay and working conditions.
ex.zh: 工会计划就工资和工作条件与管理层进行谈判。

ex.en: Wage negotiation between the union and management continued late into the night.
ex.zh: 工会与管理层的薪资谈判持续到深夜。

ex.en: The new tram line has raised property prices throughout the neighborhood.
ex.zh: 新的有轨电车线路使整个街区的房价上涨。

ex.en: Our neighbour collects the parcels whenever we are away on holiday.
ex.zh: 我们外出度假时，邻居会替我们收包裹。

senses: n. 街区；城区；邻近的地方；所在地
neighbourhood.usage: 美式拼写为neighborhood；邻居（neighbor）就是住在邻近的地方（neighbourhood）的人；美拼作neighborhood

ex.en: We grew up in the same neighbourhood.
ex.zh: 我们在同一个街区长大。

neighbourhoodneighborhood.usage: 辨析:neighbour指邻居或邻近的人或物,也指邻国;neighbourhood指城市一小块地区或某地区的人

ex.en: Volunteers in every neighbourhood helped to distribute food during the lockdown.
ex.zh: 封锁期间，每个街区的志愿者都帮忙分发食物。

ex.en: The factory closure pushed many workers to seek jobs in neighbouring counties.
ex.zh: 工厂关闭迫使许多工人前往邻县求职。

senses: pron. 两者都不,两者中无一

ex.en: Neither of the two proposed sites satisfies the safety requirements.
ex.zh: 两个拟议选址都不符合安全要求。

ex.en: My nephew has just started university, studying computer science in Manchester.
ex.zh: 我的侄子刚上大学，在曼彻斯特学习计算机科学。

senses: n. 勇气；神经；神经紧张

phrases.p: have the nerve to do sth.

ex.en: The surgeon must avoid cutting the nerve that controls hearing.
ex.zh: 外科医生必须避免切断控制听力的神经。

ex.en: It took a lot of nerve to complain directly to the manager.
ex.zh: 直接向经理投诉需要很大的勇气。

ex.en: Tests showed no damage to the nerves in her injured leg.
ex.zh: 检查显示她受伤的腿部神经没有受损。

senses: adj. 紧张不安的,神经过敏的

ex.en: Candidates often feel nervous before the oral examination, which is perfectly normal.
ex.zh: 考生在口试前感到紧张是很正常的。

phrases.m: 找鸟巢(寻找野鸟的巢并取其蛋)

ex.en: The birds abandoned their nest after the hedgerow was cut back.
ex.zh: 绿篱被修剪后，这些鸟儿抛弃了它们的巢。

ex.en: After tax, the company's net profit fell by nearly a fifth.
ex.zh: 税后，公司净利润下降了近五分之一。

ex.en: The school rebuilt its sports hall, which is now shared by the basketball and netball clubs.
ex.zh: 学校重建了体育馆，现在篮球俱乐部和无挡板篮球俱乐部共用。

senses: n. 网状物;网络;网状系统
n. （线路、道路、血管等的）网状系统；关系网；（广播或电视）网；（互联）网络
network.usage: n.网络；人际关系网；互 联网；索引p412

ex.en: This will help to grow your internal network, in addition to being a nice break in the work day.
ex.zh: 这将有助于扩展你的内部关系网，而且也是工作日的一个美好的休息时刻。

ex.en: A nationwide network of rail lines connects the port with major industrial cities.
ex.zh: 四通八达的全国铁路网将该港口与主要工业城市连接起来。

ex.en: The television network plans to broadcast the debate live across the country.
ex.zh: 这家电视网计划向全国直播这场辩论。

senses: adj. 神经的,神经系统的

ex.en: Neural implants have restored limited movement to some patients with spinal injuries.
ex.zh: 神经植入物已使一些脊髓损伤患者恢复了有限的活动能力。

senses: adj. 神经系统的；神经(病)学的

ex.en: Long-term sleep loss is linked to neurological damage according to animal studies.
ex.zh: 动物研究表明，长期睡眠不足与神经系统损伤有关。

senses: n. 神经病学家；神经科专门医师

ex.en: The neurologist recommended regular scans to monitor the progression of the disease.
ex.zh: 神经病学家建议定期扫描以监测病情进展。

ex.en: Recent advances in neurology have deepened our understanding of memory loss.
ex.zh: 神经学的最新进展加深了我们对记忆衰退的理解。

neuroscientist.usage: 词根记忆：neuro(nerve,神经)+scientist(科学家)→研究神经的科学家→神经系统科学家；索引p412

ex.en: One neuroscientist argues that sleep plays a direct role in clearing waste from the brain.
ex.zh: 一位神经科学家认为，睡眠在清除大脑废物方面起着直接作用。

senses: adj. 中立的；中性的；不受影响的
adj. 中性的；中立的；不动声色的
neutral.usage: 词根:neutr(middle中)+al(形容词后缀)→中间的→中性的；索引p412

ex.en: You might feel your heart racing or your face turning red but do whatever you can to remain neutral in both your words and actions.
ex.zh: 你可能会感到心跳加速或脸红，但尽你所能 在言语上和行动上保持中立。

ex.en: Switzerland remained neutral during both world wars, avoiding direct conflict with its neighbors.
ex.zh: 瑞士在两次世界大战期间保持中立，避免了与邻国的直接冲突。

ex.en: Reporters are expected to stay neutral and report both sides of the controversy fairly.
ex.zh: 记者应保持中立，公正地报道争议双方的观点。

ex.en: The newspaper's strict political neutrality has earned it readers from across the spectrum.
ex.zh: 这家报纸严格的政治中立为其赢得了各个派别的读者。

senses: ad. 从不；未曾；一点都不，从未

ex.en: He never imagined that his weekend hobby would turn into a full-time career.
ex.zh: 他从未想过自己的周末爱好会变成全职职业。

senses: adv. 尽管如此；不过；然而
nevertheless.usage: adv.然而，不过；副词；这类转折词常出现在完形填空题中；索引p412

ex.en: Nevertheless, the affordable housing situation is desperate.
ex.zh: 然而，经济适用房的形势很严峻。

ex.en: The experiment failed twice; nevertheless, the researchers refused to give up.
ex.zh: 实验失败了两次；尽管如此，研究人员仍拒绝放弃。

ex.en: The task was difficult; nevertheless, she managed to finish it ahead of time.
ex.zh: 任务很艰巨；尽管如此，她还是设法提前完成了。

senses: a. 新的；崭新的；新发现的；新接触的
adj. (to)不熟悉的,没有经验的,尚未习惯于

ex.en: The team is testing a new material that conducts electricity with almost no loss.
ex.zh: 该团队正在测试一种几乎无损耗导电的新材料。

books.unit: 附录 I 部分国家(或地区)名称及相关信息

ex.en: Sheep farming remains central to the economy of New Zealand despite the growth of tourism.
ex.zh: 尽管旅游业增长，养羊业仍是新西兰经济的核心。

ex.en: Newborn screening helps doctors detect rare disorders within days of birth.
ex.zh: 新生儿筛查帮助医生在出生后几天内发现罕见疾病。

ex.en: Many newlywed couples now postpone buying a home because of high deposit requirements.
ex.zh: 由于首付要求高，许多新婚夫妇现在推迟购房。

senses: n. [U] 新闻；消息；音信；新闻人物；新闻事件

ex.en: The news of the merger spread quickly through the financial markets.
ex.zh: 合并的消息在金融市场上迅速传开。

ex.en: The local newspaper investigates cases that the national media tend to overlook.
ex.zh: 这家地方报纸调查那些全国性媒体往往忽视的案件。

ex.en: Soaring newsprint costs forced several local papers to cut their print runs.
ex.zh: 新闻纸成本飙升迫使几家地方报纸削减印刷量。

senses: n. (电视台、电台或报社的)新闻编辑室

ex.en: Budget cuts have thinned the newsroom, leaving fewer reporters to cover the region.
ex.zh: 预算削减使新闻编辑室人手减少，报道该地区的记者更少了。

ex.en: She stopped at the newsstand to buy the evening paper before catching her train.
ex.zh: 赶火车之前，她在报摊停下买了份晚报。

senses: adj. 有新闻价值的；值得报道的

ex.en: Social media has blurred the line between what is newsworthy and what is merely popular.
ex.zh: 社交媒体模糊了有新闻价值与仅仅流行之间的界限。

ex.en: The next census will include detailed questions about remote working habits.
ex.zh: 下一次人口普查将包含有关远程办公习惯的详细问题。

ex.en: A nice climate and low living costs have made the city popular with retirees.
ex.zh: 宜人的气候和较低的生活成本使这座城市深受退休人士欢迎。

senses: n. 合适(称心)的工作;壁龛;(产品的)商机;适宜的小环境

ex.en: The magazine carved out a profitable niche by covering only independent cinema.
ex.zh: 这本杂志只报道独立电影，开辟出一个有利可图的细分市场。

senses: n. 镍,镍币,五分镍币,五分

ex.en: Stainless steel contains nickel, which gives it resistance to rust.
ex.zh: 不锈钢含有镍，正是镍使其具有防锈能力。

ex.en: His teammates gave him the nickname Speedy after he won three races in a single season.
ex.zh: 在他一个赛季赢了三场比赛后，队友们给他起了“飞毛腿”这个绰号。

ex.en: My niece, who is studying medicine in London, visits us every summer full of stories.
ex.zh: 我那在伦敦学医的侄女每年夏天都来看我们，带来说不尽的趣事。

ex.en: The committee worked through the night to prepare a detailed report before the deadline.
ex.zh: 委员会通宵工作，以便在截止日期前准备一份详细的报告。

nightmare.usage: night（晚上）+mare（母马）→晚上做了一大群母马狂奔而来的梦→噩梦

ex.en: Losing all the research data on the eve of submission was every scholar's nightmare.
ex.zh: 在提交前夕丢失全部研究数据是每位学者最害怕的噩梦。

ex.en: Passengers described nightmarish queues at the airport after the computer system crashed.
ex.zh: 计算机系统崩溃后，乘客形容机场排队如同噩梦。

ex.en: The museum opens at nine and closes at five, so visitors have plenty of time.
ex.zh: 博物馆九点开门，五点闭馆，所以参观者有充足的时间。

ex.en: She left her village at nineteen to seek a better education in the capital.
ex.zh: 她十九岁离开家乡，去首都寻求更好的教育。

ex.en: Nearly ninety percent of the students surveyed said they preferred online lectures.
ex.zh: 接受调查的学生中有近百分之九十表示更喜欢在线课程。

ex.en: Nitrogen makes up about seventy-eight percent of the air we breathe.
ex.zh: 氮约占我们呼吸的空气的百分之七十八。

ex.en: Farmers apply nitrogen fertilisers to boost crop yields.
ex.zh: 农民施用氮肥来提高作物产量。

ex.en: Liquid nitrogen is used to freeze biological samples for storage.
ex.zh: 液氮被用于冷冻生物样本以便储存。

ex.en: There is no simple answer to the question of how technology reshapes human relationships.
ex.zh: 关于技术如何重塑人际关系这一问题，并没有简单的答案。

senses: n. (the ~)贵族；高尚的思想或品格

ex.en: The novel portrays the decline of the nobility and the rise of a wealthy merchant class.
ex.zh: 这部小说描绘了贵族阶层的衰落和富商阶层的兴起。

senses: adj. 崇高的，高尚的；贵族的，高贵的
noble.usage: 发音类似“诺贝尔”→诺贝尔捐财产设奖→高尚的；索引p412

ex.en: He was a young man of noble birth.
ex.zh: 他是个出身高贵的年轻人。

ex.en: It was noble of her to donate the prize money to the local children's hospital.
ex.zh: 她把奖金捐给当地儿童医院，行为十分高尚。

ex.en: The novel portrays a noble knight who defends the poor against unjust lords.
ex.zh: 这部小说塑造了一位保卫穷人、反抗不公领主的高贵骑士。

senses: n. [C] 小人物，无足轻重的人
n. 小人物,无足轻重的人

ex.en: Nobody in the audience expected the quiet young researcher to challenge the established theory.
ex.zh: 没有一个观众会想到这位安静的年轻研究者会挑战已有的理论。

ex.en: The court ruled that the company was innocent of knowingly polluting the river.
ex.zh: 法庭裁定该公司没有故意污染河流的罪名。

senses: n. 点头招呼;打盹,瞌睡

ex.en: When the chairman nodded, the speakers knew their proposals had won cautious approval.
ex.zh: 主席点头时，发言者们知道他们的提案获得了谨慎的认可。

ex.en: The constant noise from the construction site made it difficult for residents to concentrate.
ex.zh: 建筑工地持续的噪声使居民难以集中注意力。

ex.en: The library banned all noise-making devices, including phones, after complaints from students.
ex.zh: 在学生投诉后，图书馆禁止所有发出噪音的设备，包括手机。

ex.en: Protesters marched noisily past the embassy, waving banners and beating drums.
ex.zh: 抗议者挥舞旗帜、敲着鼓，吵闹地从大使馆外经过。

ex.en: The noisiness of open-plan offices is a common complaint in workplace surveys.
ex.zh: 开放式办公室的嘈杂是职场调查中常见的抱怨。

senses: a. 吵闹的；嘈杂的；充满噪声的；吵吵闹闹的

ex.en: Children learn better in quiet classrooms than in noisy, overcrowded ones.
ex.zh: 儿童在安静的教室里比在嘈杂拥挤的教室里学得更好。

senses: adj. 名义上的,有名无实的
adj. (余额、租金)微不足道的,象征性的

ex.en: He remains the nominal head of the company, though real decisions are made by the board.
ex.zh: 他仍然是公司名义上的负责人，尽管真正的决策由董事会做出。

nominate.usage: 辨析:appoint指任命委任,常与as或to be连用;nominate指任命提名,常与for,as连用

ex.en: The party has decided to nominate a relatively unknown candidate for the presidential election.
ex.zh: 该党已决定提名一位相对不知名的候选人参加总统选举。

ex.en: The finding was dismissed as nonsense by reviewers who repeated the experiment carefully.
ex.zh: 仔细重复该实验的审稿人认为这一发现是无稽之谈。

senses: adj. 非人类的；非人类制造的

ex.en: Tool use was once considered proof of a divide between human and non-human animals.
ex.zh: 使用工具曾被认为是人类与非人类动物之间分界的证据。

ex.en: The movement appeals to non-materialistic consumers who value experiences over possessions.
ex.zh: 这场运动吸引了重视体验而非物质财富的非物质主义消费者。

senses: a. 非营利的；不以营利为目的的

ex.en: The non-profit sector now employs more people than the country's entire manufacturing industry.
ex.zh: 非营利部门现在的雇员人数已超过该国整个制造业。

ex.en: Linguists argue that non-standard dialects follow grammatical rules of their own.
ex.zh: 语言学家认为，非标准方言自有其语法规则。

senses: adj. 无经济价值的；非商业的

ex.en: The website publishes noncommercial articles written by volunteers from different academic fields.
ex.zh: 该网站刊登由来自不同学术领域的志愿者撰写的非商业性文章。

senses: n. 不顺从一般公认信念、习惯的人

ex.en: The company was founded by a nonconformist who rejected the industry's usual way of doing business.
ex.zh: 这家公司由一位拒绝行业惯常经营方式的不循规蹈矩者创立。

ex.en: The committee chose a noncontroversial topic so that every member could reach agreement quickly.
ex.zh: 委员会选择了一个不会引起争议的话题，以便每位成员都能迅速达成一致。

senses: pron. 没有人,没有任何东西
pron. ……中任何一个都不;谁也不
none.usage: 词组:none but只有,除了……;none the less然而,虽然如此,依然

ex.en: None of the explanations offered so far fully accounts for the decline in bee populations.
ex.zh: 迄今提出的解释没有一个能完全说明蜜蜂数量减少的原因。

ex.en: The report examines noneconomic factors, such as culture and trust, that shape trade relations.
ex.zh: 该报告考察了影响贸易关系的文化、信任等非经济因素。

ex.en: The evidence was incomplete; it was nonetheless compelling.
ex.zh: 证据虽不完整，但仍然很有说服力。

ex.en: The task seemed impossible; she nonetheless finished it ahead of schedule.
ex.zh: 这项任务看似不可能完成；尽管如此，她还是提前完成了。

ex.en: Ticket sales were slow; the show was nonetheless extended for another month.
ex.zh: 售票进展缓慢；尽管如此，演出还是延长了一个月。

senses: n. 胡说,废话,无意义的言谈或文字
n. 谬论，胡扯，毫无意义的话
nonsense.usage: 助记:non(否定)+sense(辨别)→胡说;派生nonsensical无意义的,荒谬的；non(否定前缀)+sense(感觉,意识)→没有常识的→胡扯；索引p412

ex.en: There is a great deal of this kind of nonsense in the medical journals.
ex.zh: 医学期刊中充斥着这类无稽之谈。

ex.en: The report dismissed the rumor as complete nonsense.
ex.zh: 报告斥这一传言纯属无稽之谈。

ex.en: He talked nonsense for ten minutes before anyone challenged his figures.
ex.zh: 他胡扯了十分钟，才有人质疑他的数据。

senses: adj. 不使用语言表达的

ex.en: Skilled negotiators pay close attention to nonverbal signals such as posture and eye contact.
ex.zh: 熟练的谈判者会密切关注姿态和眼神接触等非语言信号。

ex.en: Sales of instant noodles rose sharply during the recession as families cut spending on restaurants.
ex.zh: 经济衰退期间，随着家庭削减外出就餐的开支，方便面的销量急剧上升。

ex.en: The press conference is scheduled for noon, shortly after the cabinet meeting ends.
ex.zh: 新闻发布会定在中午举行，就在内阁会议结束后不久。

ex.en: The survey neither identifies the causes of stress nor suggests practical remedies.
ex.zh: 这项调查既没有找出压力的成因，也没有提出切实可行的补救办法。

senses: n. 标准，规范；（统计学中的）平均值

ex.en: Working from home has become the norm rather than the exception in many industries.
ex.zh: 在许多行业，居家办公已成为常态而非例外。

ex.en: Cultural norms about punctuality differ widely from one country to another.
ex.zh: 关于守时的文化规范因国家而异，差别很大。

ex.en: By the age of thirty, his earnings were well above the national norm.
ex.zh: 到三十岁时，他的收入已远高于全国平均水平。

normal.usage: adj.正常的，普通的 n.常态，通常标准；索引p412

ex.en: It is perfectly normal to feel anxious before an important examination.
ex.zh: 在重要考试前感到焦虑是完全正常的。

ex.en: Life in the town gradually returned to normal after the flood waters receded.
ex.zh: 洪水退去后，镇上的生活逐渐恢复正常。

ex.en: The patient's temperature is back to normal, and the doctor discharged her this morning.
ex.zh: 病人体温已恢复正常，医生今早让她出院了。

ex.en: The normalization of diplomatic relations opened new markets for companies on both sides.
ex.zh: 外交关系的正常化为双方企业开辟了新市场。

ex.en: The library normally closes at ten, but it stays open longer during exam weeks.
ex.zh: 图书馆通常十点闭馆，但在考试周会延长开放时间。

ex.en: Many birds fly north in spring and return to warmer regions before winter arrives.
ex.zh: 许多鸟春天飞往北方，在冬天来临前返回较温暖的地区。

north america.usage: 附录Ⅱ 大洲名；形容词 North American

ex.en: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles across North America each autumn.
ex.zh: 每年秋天，帝王蝶迁徙数千英里横跨北美洲。

ex.en: The North American market accounts for roughly half of the firm's annual sales.
ex.zh: 北美市场约占该公司年销售额的一半。

ex.en: The northeast of the country has attracted heavy industry because of its rich coal deposits.
ex.zh: 该国东北部因煤炭资源丰富而吸引了重工业。

ex.en: Northern cities have invested heavily in public transport to reduce traffic congestion.
ex.zh: 北方城市已在公共交通上投入巨资，以缓解交通拥堵。

ex.en: The company plans to expand its distribution network across the northwest next year.
ex.zh: 该公司计划明年将其分销网络扩展到整个西北地区。

books.unit: 附录 I 部分国家(或地区)名称及相关信息

ex.en: Norway generates nearly all of its electricity from renewable hydropower.
ex.zh: 挪威几乎全部电力都来自可再生的水力发电。

senses: n. 鼻；鼻子；（飞机、太空船等的）头部，头锥
n. 鼻子;(飞机、船等的)前端;突出部分

ex.en: The dog followed the scent with its nose close to the ground until it found the lost hiker.
ex.zh: 那条狗鼻子贴近地面循着气味追踪，最终找到了迷路的远足者。

senses: adj. 怀旧的,乡愁的,令人怀念的

ex.en: The old photographs made the audience nostalgic for an era before digital technology.
ex.zh: 这些老照片使观众怀念起数字技术出现之前的时代。

ex.en: The new policy does not apply to small businesses with fewer than ten employees.
ex.zh: 新政策不适用于雇员少于十人的小企业。

senses: adj. 显著的,值得注意的
adj. 显著的，值得注意的
notable.usage: not（=note注意；记录）+able（能……的）→能注意到的→显著的

ex.en: It is notable that only 15% of senior managers are women.
ex.zh: 值得注意的是，高级经理中只有15%是女性。

ex.en: The city has undergone a notable transformation since the new metro opened.
ex.zh: 自新地铁开通以来，这座城市发生了显著的变化。

ex.en: The conference attracted notable speakers from industry and academia.
ex.zh: 会议邀请了来自产业界和学术界的知名演讲者。

ex.en: Living standards in the region have improved notably over the past decade.
ex.zh: 过去十年，该地区的生活水平显著提高。

ex.en: Several speakers, most notably the former minister, opposed the plan.
ex.zh: 几位发言者——尤其是前部长——反对这项计划。

ex.en: House prices in the capital rose notably faster than in other regions.
ex.zh: 首都的房价上涨明显快于其他地区。

ex.en: Copies of the deed were certified by a notary before being filed with the court.
ex.zh: 契约副本经公证人认证后才提交法院存档。

senses: n. 注释,评注(c);短信,便条(c);钞票,纸币(c)
v. 记下,摘下;指出,特别提到;注意,留意
note.usage: take/make notes 记笔记；n.便条；笔记；注释；音符 v.留意，注意；指出，表明；记 录，记下；索引p412

ex.en: Studying Scovell's papers at the Public Record Office, London, I found that he had left an extensive journal and copious notes about his work in the Peninsula.
ex.zh: 在伦敦公共档案馆研究斯科维尔的资料时,我发现他留下了在半岛工作时的大量日记和丰富笔记。

ex.en: The longest bull run in a century of art-market history ended on a dramatic note with a sale of 56 works by Damien Hirst.
ex.zh: 达米恩·赫斯特的56幅艺术品的拍卖标志着艺术品市场一个世纪以来最为持久的“牛市”戏剧性地落下帷幕。

ex.en: Please note that the library closes earlier than usual during the examination period.
ex.zh: 请注意，考试期间图书馆闭馆时间比平时早。

senses: n. [C] 笔记本；笔记本电脑

ex.en: She filled a whole notebook with observations collected during her fieldwork in the mountains.
ex.zh: 她在山区实地考察期间收集的观察记录写满了整整一个笔记本。

senses: a. 显著的；值得注意的；重要的
adj. 显著的,值得注意的
adj. 值得注意的，显著的；重要的

ex.en: It is noteworthy that only 15% of senior managers are women.
ex.zh: 值得注意的是，只有15%的高级管理人员是女性。

ex.en: The study produced several noteworthy findings about sleep patterns among teenagers.
ex.zh: 这项研究得出了若干关于青少年睡眠模式的值得注意的发现。

ex.en: It is noteworthy that the two independently conducted surveys reached almost identical conclusions.
ex.zh: 值得注意的是，两项独立开展的调查得出了几乎相同的结论。

senses: pron. 没有什么；无关紧要的东西；毫无趣味的事
pron. 没有什么东西,什么也没有
nothing.usage: be nothing to对...无所谓;have nothing to do with与...无关

ex.en: Nothing in the report suggests that the company deliberately ignored safety standards.
ex.zh: 报告中没有任何内容表明该公司蓄意忽视安全标准。

notice.usage: come into notice引起注意；n.注意，察觉；布告 v.意识，注意；索引p413

ex.en: It takes about three weeks to a month to notice any significant changes in your weight due to altering your training program.
ex.zh: 由于改变了训练计划，大约花三周到一个月的时间，你才能注意到体重方面的任何明显变化。

ex.en: Employees must give at least one month's notice before leaving the company.
ex.zh: 员工离职必须至少提前一个月通知。

ex.en: Did you notice that the shop has put up a notice about the changed opening hours?
ex.zh: 你注意到店里贴出了关于营业时间变更的通知了吗？

senses: adj. 显而易见的，显著的

ex.en: There is a noticeable difference between the two brands.
ex.zh: 这两个品牌有明显的区别。

ex.en: Customers must give written notification at least fourteen days before cancelling the service.
ex.zh: 客户取消服务前必须至少提前十四天发出书面通知。

phrases.p: notify sb. of sth./notify sth. to sb.

notify.usage: 辨析:notify搭配notify sb. of sth.,宾语后可接不定式或从句;inform搭配inform sb. of sth.；索引p412

ex.en: Competition winners will be notified by post.
ex.zh: 将发信通知竞赛的优胜者。

ex.en: Customers must notify the bank immediately if their cards are lost or stolen.
ex.zh: 客户的银行卡遗失或被盗必须立即通知银行。

ex.en: Schools are required to notify parents of any changes to the examination schedule.
ex.zh: 学校须将考试日程的任何变动通知家长。

senses: n. 信念，观念，想法；理解
notion.usage: n.概念，想法；发音类似“闹心”→女儿长大后离家远工作的“想法”让我很闹心→想法，观念。；词根:not(know知道)+(t)ion(名词后缀)→知道某件事后对其产生了看法→看法；索引p413

ex.en: Online culture thinks highly of the notion that the information flowing onto the screen comes there by specific request.
ex.zh: 网上文化推崇这样一种理念，即在你提出具体的要求之后，信息才会出现在屏幕上。

ex.en: The notion that money can buy happiness has been questioned by many psychologists.
ex.zh: 金钱能买到幸福的观念受到许多心理学家的质疑。

ex.en: He rejected the notion that children learn best without any guidance from adults.
ex.zh: 他反对那种认为儿童在没有任何成人指导下学习效果最好的观点。

senses: a. 臭名昭著的；声名狼藉的
adj. 声名狼藉的，臭名昭著的
notorious.usage: not（知道）+ori+-ous→坏得出名的→臭名昭著的。反famous a.著名的（褒义）；同义infamous;反义famous；no（没有）+tori（联想成story"故事"）+ous（形容词后缀）→身上没有什么好故事的→声名狼藉的，臭名昭著的

ex.en: Today, two years after the death of the notorious dictator, the house, which he used as an office, is opening as a visitor attraction.
ex.zh: 如今，在这位臭名昭著的独裁者去世两年后，这座他曾用作办公室的房子开始作为游客景点开放。

ex.en: The region is notorious for its terrible traffic congestion during rush hours.
ex.zh: 该地区因高峰时段严重的交通拥堵而声名狼藉。

ex.en: He is a notorious liar whose stories can never be trusted.
ex.zh: 他是个臭名昭著的骗子，他讲的话永远不可信。

ex.en: Reform has been vigorously opposed, perhaps most notoriously in education, where charter schools, academies and merit pay all faced drawn-out battles.
ex.zh: 改革一直遭到强烈反对，或许最为人知的当属教育改革，其中特许学校、专科院校以及绩效工资等方面都面临持久战。

ex.en: Notwithstanding the heavy rain, thousands of fans gathered outside the stadium before dawn.
ex.zh: 尽管大雨倾盆，数千名球迷仍在黎明前聚集在体育场外。

ex.en: In English, a noun can function as the subject or the object of a sentence.
ex.zh: 在英语中，名词可以充当句子的主语或宾语。

senses: vt. 培养，助长（情绪、观点等）
nourish.usage: 近义：nurture vt. 养育；培养；nouri（养育）+-sh→给营养→滋养。族nourishment n.营养品；nourishing a.滋养的；派生nourishing滋养的;nourishment食物,滋养品,养料；nouris（联想成 nurse 培育）+h→抚养，培养

ex.en: By investing in education, we nourish the talents of our children.
ex.zh: 我们通过教育投资，培养孩子们的才能。

ex.en: All the children were well nourished and in good physical condition.
ex.zh: 所有这些孩子都营养良好，身体健康。

ex.en: A good breakfast nourishes the body and prepares the mind for the day.
ex.zh: 一顿好的早餐滋养身体，让大脑为一天做好准备。

ex.en: The final report is due in November, after the consultation period ends.
ex.zh: 征求意见期结束后，最终报告定于十一月提交。

ex.en: A sudden brightening of the star indicated that a nova had occurred.
ex.zh: 这颗恒星突然变亮表明发生了一次新星爆发。

novel.usage: 辨析:novel指事物与众不同、新奇;fresh指清新有活力或人无经验;new指未用过、刚出现,一般用语；n.(长篇)小说 adj.新颖的，珍奇的；nov（=new"新的"）+el→新的东西→新颖的；索引p413

ex.en: It tried to implement a novel financial aid program.
ex.zh: 它试图实施一项新的财政援助计划。

ex.en: science fiction novels // comic novels
ex.zh: 科幻小说 // 喜剧小说

ex.en: The team proposed a novel approach to storing solar energy in liquid form.
ex.zh: 团队提出了一种以液体形式储存太阳能的新颖方法。

ex.en: The novelist drew on her childhood in a mining town for the new book.
ex.zh: 这位小说家的新书取材于她在矿业小镇度过的童年。

novelty.usage: 同根:novice初学者,新手;innovate改革,革新;renovate修复,革新；索引p413

ex.en: Novelty itself frequently provokes disbelief.
ex.zh: 新奇的事物本身经常引起怀疑。

ex.en: Wearing smart glasses was a novelty at first, but people soon lost interest.
ex.zh: 起初戴智能眼镜很新奇，但人们很快就失去了兴趣。

ex.en: The novelty of the design attracted many young customers to the store.
ex.zh: 设计的新颖吸引了许多年轻顾客来到这家商店。

ex.en: The final version of the agreement is expected to be signed in November.
ex.zh: 协定的最终版本预计将于十一月签署。

ex.en: Now that the data have been verified, the team can begin drafting its final report.
ex.zh: 既然数据已得到核实，团队就可以开始起草最终报告了。

nowadays.usage: 辨析:now含义更广,可指说话此刻;nowadays常用于现今与旧时习俗对比,带感情色彩

ex.en: Nowadays, many employees expect flexible hours rather than higher salaries.
ex.zh: 如今，许多员工期望弹性工作时间而不是更高的薪水。

senses: adv. 任何地方都不,哪都没有
nowhere.usage: 助记:no(没有)+where(在哪里)→哪都没有,没有地方；adv.无处，哪里都不；没有任 何地方 n.不存在的地方

ex.en: Without a clear plan, the project seemed to be going nowhere.
ex.zh: 没有明确的计划，这个项目似乎毫无进展。

ex.en: The village is nowhere near the industrial centers of the country.
ex.zh: 这个村庄离该国的工业中心很远。

ex.en: He searched everywhere for the missing file, but it was nowhere to be found.
ex.zh: 他到处寻找丢失的文件，却哪儿也找不到。

senses: adj. 原子能的，核能的；核武器的
nuclear.usage: nuclear family核心家庭；adj.核子的，原子核的；拓展：a nuclear reactor 核反应堆；索引p413

ex.en: Nuclear power is cleaner than coal.
ex.zh: 核能比煤更清洁。

ex.en: Some countries are investing heavily in nuclear energy to cut carbon emissions.
ex.zh: 一些国家正在大力投资核能以减少碳排放。

ex.en: The agreement aims to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons around the world.
ex.zh: 该协议旨在防止核武器在世界各地扩散。

ex.en: A small group of experienced engineers formed the nucleus of the new research team.
ex.zh: 一小批经验丰富的工程师组成了新研究团队的核心。

ex.en: Default options can nudge employees into saving more for retirement.
ex.zh: 默认选项可以促使员工为退休储蓄更多。

senses: n. 讨厌的人（或东西）；麻烦事
n. 妨害行为；麻烦事；讨厌的人(或东西)

ex.en: I don't want to be a nuisance so tell me if you want to be alone.
ex.zh: 我不想讨人嫌，你要是想一个人待着就说一声。

ex.en: Constant calls from insurance salesmen are a real nuisance.
ex.zh: 保险推销员接连不断的电话真是烦人。

ex.en: The noise from the construction site became a nuisance to local residents.
ex.zh: 建筑工地的噪音成了当地居民的一桩麻烦事。

senses: adj. 麻木的,失去感觉的
vt. 使麻木,使失去感觉

ex.en: After hours in the freezing wind, her fingers were numb and she could barely hold the pen.
ex.zh: 在寒风中待了几个小时后，她的手指冻得麻木，几乎握不住笔。

ex.en: A growing number of consumers are willing to pay more for environmentally friendly products.
ex.zh: 越来越多的消费者愿意为环保产品支付更高的价格。

ex.en: Numerous small businesses closed during the recession, despite government support schemes.
ex.zh: 尽管有政府扶持计划，众多小企业仍在衰退期间倒闭。

senses: adj. 数字的,用数表示的
adj. 数字的；用数字表示的
numerical.usage: 助记:numer(数字)+ical(形容词后缀)→数字的;派生numerically adv.在数量上；索引p413

ex.en: The survey data were converted into numerical form for statistical analysis.
ex.zh: 调查数据被转换成数字形式以便进行统计分析。

ex.en: Children develop basic numerical skills long before they start school.
ex.zh: 孩子们在上学之前很久就发展出基本的数字技能。

ex.en: The defenders had a clear numerical advantage over the attacking army.
ex.zh: 守军在数量上明显多于进攻的军队。

senses: adj. 许多的,众多的,大批的
numerous.usage: 助记:numer(数字)+ous(形容词后缀)→数字大的→大量的；numer（联想number“数字”）+ous（形容词后缀）→数量多的→许多的。；索引p413

ex.en: This scale took numerous factors into consideration.
ex.zh: 这个量表考虑了许多因素。

ex.en: Numerous studies have linked long working hours to an increased risk of heart disease.
ex.zh: 大量研究表明，长时间工作与心脏病风险增加有关。

ex.en: The museum has received numerous complaints about the new admission policy.
ex.zh: 博物馆已收到大量针对新门票政策的投诉。

ex.en: The nurse monitored the patient's temperature every two hours and recorded the results carefully.
ex.zh: 护士每两小时监测一次病人的体温，并仔细记录结果。

senses: n. 托儿所,保育室;苗圃,繁殖场
nursery.usage: nurs（养育，护理）+ery（场所，地点）→养育孩子的地方→托儿所

ex.en: The children are at nursery three days a week.
ex.zh: 孩子们每周上3天托儿所。

ex.en: Working parents increasingly rely on nurseries to care for their young children.
ex.zh: 职场父母越来越依赖托儿所照看年幼的孩子。

ex.en: The hospital bought young trees from a local nursery for its garden.
ex.zh: 医院从当地苗圃购买了幼树用于庭院绿化。

ex.en: School meals were redesigned to improve nutrition among children from low-income families.
ex.zh: 学校膳食经过重新设计，以改善低收入家庭儿童的营养状况。

senses: vt. 养育,教养,教育(儿童)
vt. 培育,培养(某物);滋养;扶植;支持
nurture.usage: nourish 的近义词；nurs（养育）+-ture→养育。心理学名词短语nature versus nurture先天对后天；同义care,encouragement,support；nutrient 拓展词；索引p413

ex.en: In place of Thomas Carlyle, Britain nurtured Christopher Hill, EP Thompson and Eric Hobsbawm.
ex.zh: 英国培养出了克里斯托弗·希尔、E.P.汤普森和埃里克·霍布斯鲍姆，他们取代了托马斯·克莱尔。

ex.en: Parents and schools share the responsibility to nurture children's creativity.
ex.zh: 家长和学校共同承担着培养孩子创造力的责任。

ex.en: The debate over whether nature or nurture shapes personality remains unsettled.
ex.zh: 关于天性还是养育塑造人格的争论仍未平息。

senses: n. 坚果;螺母,螺帽;难题

ex.en: Squirrels store nuts in autumn to survive the cold months when food is scarce.
ex.zh: 松鼠在秋天储存坚果，以度过食物匮乏的寒冷月份。

ex.en: Plants draw minerals and other nutrients from the soil.
ex.zh: 植物从土壤中吸取矿物质和其他养分。

ex.en: Fruit and vegetables are rich in nutrients that protect the body against disease.
ex.zh: 水果和蔬菜富含帮助人体抵御疾病的营养物质。

ex.en: A balanced diet should supply all the essential nutrients the body needs.
ex.zh: 均衡的饮食应提供身体所需的全部必需营养素。

senses: n. 营养，滋养；营养的补给
nutrition.usage: 助记:nutri(营养)+tion(名词后缀)→营养；nut(坚果)+ri(日)+tion(名词后缀)→每日吃点坚果补充"营养"；索引p413

ex.en: Nutrition information is now provided on the back of most food products.
ex.zh: 现在大多数食品的背面都有营养信息。

ex.en: Mental health is like the immune system of the body, which under stress or through lack of nutrition or exercise can be weakened, but which never leaves us.
ex.zh: 心理健康就像身体的免疫系统，在面临压力、营养不足或缺乏运动时会被削弱，但却从不会离我们而去。

ex.en: A balanced diet provides the nutrition that growing children need for physical and mental development.
ex.zh: 均衡的饮食提供成长中的儿童身心发育所需的营养。

ex.en: Adapt your usual eating regime to make it more nutritious.
ex.zh: 调整你的日常饮食习惯，使之更富有营养。

ex.en: Early nylon stockings were so popular that stores often sold out within hours.
ex.zh: 早期的尼龙袜非常受欢迎，商店常常几小时内就销售一空。

ex.en: The antique table, carved from solid oak, has survived three generations of the family.
ex.zh: 这张用实心橡木雕制的古董桌子已经陪伴了这个家族三代人。

phrases.m: 多嘴,插嘴,插手,多管闲事

ex.en: The rowers lifted their oars in unison, and the boat glided silently across the lake.
ex.zh: 桨手们整齐地举起船桨，小船悄然滑过湖面。

ex.en: Trade caravans crossed the desert only between one oasis and the next.
ex.zh: 商队穿越沙漠时只能从一个绿洲走到下一个绿洲。

ex.en: Breakfast cereals made from oats are marketed as a way to lower cholesterol.
ex.zh: 燕麦早餐谷物被宣传为降低胆固醇的一种方式。

senses: n. 誓言,宣誓(c);咒骂,诅咒语
oath.usage: 复数oaths。近pledge n.誓言；vow n.誓约。give evidence on oath宣誓作证；n.誓言，誓约；诅咒，咒骂

ex.en: Judges must take an oath to uphold the law before taking office.
ex.zh: 法官就职前必须宣誓维护法律。

ex.en: Every witness has to swear an oath before giving evidence in court.
ex.zh: 每个证人在法庭作证前都必须宣誓。

ex.en: The new president swore the oath of office before a huge crowd.
ex.zh: 新总统在众人面前宣读了就职誓言。

senses: 加强意义；相反；在……上面；对面

ex.en: Bureaucratic delays remain the chief obstacle to foreign investment in the region.
ex.zh: 官僚程序拖延仍是该地区外国投资的主要障碍。

ex.en: In traditional families, children were once expected to show complete obedience to their parents.
ex.zh: 在传统家庭中，孩子曾被要求完全服从父母。

ex.en: The soldiers were drilled in discipline and instant obedience to orders.
ex.zh: 士兵们接受纪律和立即服从命令的训练。

ex.en: Blind obedience to authority can prevent people from questioning harmful policies.
ex.zh: 对权威的盲目服从会妨碍人们质疑有害的政策。

obedient.usage: obedi（=obey“服从”）+ent（具有……性质的）→服从的。

ex.en: As a child she was quiet and obedient, always doing what her teachers asked.
ex.zh: 小时候她安静听话，总是按老师的要求去做。

ex.en: An obedient dog responds to its owner's commands at once.
ex.zh: 听话的狗会立刻响应主人的指令。

ex.en: The new manager does not want a team of obedient staff who never offer new ideas.
ex.zh: 这位新经理不想要一支只会服从、从不提出新想法的团队。

ex.en: The proportion of obese adults has doubled since the survey began in the 1990s.
ex.zh: 自二十世纪九十年代调查开始以来，肥胖成年人的比例翻了一番。

ex.en: Regular exercise and a healthy diet are the most effective weapons against obesity.
ex.zh: 定期锻炼和健康饮食是对抗肥胖最有效的武器。

ex.en: Childhood obesity has become a serious public health problem in many countries.
ex.zh: 儿童肥胖已成为许多国家严重的公共健康问题。

ex.en: Doctors warn that obesity greatly increases the risk of heart disease and diabetes.
ex.zh: 医生警告说，肥胖会大大增加患心脏病和糖尿病的风险。

senses: v. 服从,遵从;听由,听从摆布
obey.usage: obey 及物动词直接接宾语；obedience n. 服从。；索引p413

ex.en: Soldiers are trained to obey orders.
ex.zh: 士兵被训练服从命令。

ex.en: Drivers who fail to obey traffic signals put everyone on the road at risk.
ex.zh: 不遵守交通信号的司机使路上的每个人都面临危险。

ex.en: The court ruled that the company had refused to obey the safety regulations.
ex.zh: 法院裁定该公司拒不遵守安全法规。

object.usage: 辨析:object指行为、感觉、思索的对象；subject指批评、学习、调查及用以实验的对象；词根词缀法：ob（表示“方向”）+ject（抛，扔）→朝……方向扔东西→反对。；ob（方向）+ject（抛，扔）→朝某方向扔东西→反对；object to 中的 to 是介词，后接名词/动名词；objection n. 反对。

ex.en: Members of the council strongly objected to plans to sell off the land.
ex.zh: 委员会成员强烈反对出售土地的计划。

ex.en: Many parents object to this teaching method.
ex.zh: 许多家长反对这种教学方法。

ex.en: First, the object of our study pleads for definition.
ex.zh: 首先，我们需要定义所研究的对象。

objection.usage: objection后接介词to，to后接名词、动名词或代词；n.反对的理由；异议；索引p413

ex.en: The main objection to the plan is its likely impact on the local environment.
ex.zh: 对该计划的主要反对意见是它可能对当地环境造成影响。

ex.en: He raised no objection when the meeting was moved to Friday afternoon.
ex.zh: 会议改到周五下午时，他没有表示反对。

ex.en: Despite fierce objection from residents, the council approved the construction of the new road.
ex.zh: 尽管居民强烈反对，议会还是批准了新道路的修建。

senses: adj. 引起反对的,讨厌的

ex.en: The advertising watchdog ruled that the campaign's comparison with rivals was objectionable and misleading.
ex.zh: 广告监管机构裁定该广告活动与对手的比较令人反感且有误导性。

senses: adj. 客观的，如实的，无偏见的
objective.usage: 辨析:aim指确定并愿为之努力的目的；goal须经坚持不懈努力才能达成；objective指具体、直接、很快可达到的目的；purpose指意图、打算；n.目的，目标；宾格 adj.客观的，不带个人情感的； 宾格的；索引p413

ex.en: In order to achieve these objectives, we must concentrate more on co-productions, the exchange of news, documentary services and training.
ex.zh: 为了实现这些目标，我们必须更加关注联合制作、新闻的交流、纪录片服务和培训。

ex.en: Objective thinking may boost inventiveness.
ex.zh: 客观的思考可以促进发明创造。

ex.en: The primary objective of the reform is to make health care affordable for all.
ex.zh: 改革的首要目标是让所有人都能负担得起医疗保健。

ex.en: Nurses' pay cannot be assessed objectively without reliable data on workload and outcomes.
ex.zh: 没有关于工作量和成效的可靠数据，就无法客观评估护士的薪酬。

ex.en: Critics questioned the objectiveness of a study funded entirely by the drinks industry.
ex.zh: 批评者质疑一项完全由饮料行业资助的研究的客观性。

ex.en: A good journalist must report the news with complete objectivity.
ex.zh: 优秀的记者必须以完全客观的态度报道新闻。

ex.en: The committee's objectivity was questioned because several members had financial ties to the company.
ex.zh: 委员会的客观性受到质疑，因为几名成员与该公司存在经济利益关联。

ex.en: Historians strive for objectivity when they interpret past events.
ex.zh: 历史学家在解释过去的事件时力求客观。

phrases.p: have an obligation to do sth.

obligation.usage: [族] oblige vt. 迫使；oblige 的派生词；n.义务，责任；索引p413

ex.en: Parents have a legal obligation to ensure that their children receive an education.
ex.zh: 父母有确保子女接受教育的法律义务。

ex.en: Companies are under increasing obligation to protect the personal data of their users.
ex.zh: 公司承担着保护用户个人数据的越来越大的义务。

ex.en: He felt a moral obligation to help his neighbor after the flood.
ex.zh: 洪水过后，他觉得有道义责任帮助邻居。

ex.en: The introductory course is obligatory for all students, whatever their chosen specialism.
ex.zh: 导论课对所有学生都是必修的，无论其选择什么专业。

oblige.usage: oblig（束缚）+e→绑住→迫使。族：obligation n. 义务；责任。近义：compel vt. 迫使；发音类似“我不来这”→我不想来这，但是又不得不来→迫使，强迫。；词根记忆：ob(表加强)+lig(bind,捆绑)+e→用力捆绑→迫使；索引p413

ex.en: Getting a DNT signal does not oblige anyone to stop tracking, although some companies have promised to do so.
ex.zh: 尽管一些公司已经承诺会停止追踪，但收到DNT信号并不会迫使任何人（企业）停止追踪。

ex.en: The law obliges companies to publish detailed reports on their carbon emissions.
ex.zh: 法律要求公司公布其碳排放的详细报告。

ex.en: We were obliged to cancel the outdoor event because of the storm.
ex.zh: 由于暴风雨，我们不得不取消户外活动。

senses: a. 令人震惊的；淫秽的，下流的；（数量等）大得惊人的，骇人听闻的
adj. 淫秽的;猥亵的;下流的;骇人听闻的
obscene.usage: ob-（向）+scen（污染）+e→被污染的→下流的。族obscenity n.淫秽；猥亵言语

ex.en: Critics argued that the executive's obscene salary was unjustifiable while the company cut jobs.
ex.zh: 批评者认为，在公司裁员之际，这位高管高得惊人的薪水是不合理的。

senses: adj. 无名的；鲜为人知的；费解的；难以理解的
v. 使模糊；使隐晦；使费解
obscure.usage: 辨析:obscure指物体或观点不清晰、难理解；ambiguous指有两种以上解释、模棱两可；vague指因光线暗淡或过于笼统而不清楚；adj.鲜为人知的；费解的，晦涩 的 v.遮掩，遮蔽；使费解；ob(不)+scure(联想sure确切的)→不确切的→费解的，难以理解的；索引p413

ex.en: He could not analyze carefully what this obscure officer may or may not have contributed to that great struggle between nations or indeed tell us anything much about the man himself.
ex.zh: 他无法仔细分析这位默默无闻的军官是否对那场国家间的伟大斗争有所贡献，也无法确切地告诉我们关于他本人的任何情况。

ex.en: At the same time, Dickens submitted short sketches to obscure magazines.
ex.zh: 与此同时，狄更斯向一些不知名的杂志投递了一些短篇随笔。

ex.en: submit short sketches to obscure magazines
ex.zh: 向不知名的杂志投递一些短篇随笔

senses: adj. 能看得到的;能察觉到的
observable.usage: adj.显著的；觉察得到的；看得 见的；索引p413

ex.en: There is no observable difference in quality between the two products.
ex.zh: 这两种产品在质量上看不出差别。

ex.en: The effects of the new policy became observable within a few months.
ex.zh: 新政策的效果在几个月内就显现出来。

ex.en: Scientists must base their conclusions on observable evidence rather than personal belief.
ex.zh: 科学家的结论必须基于可观察到的证据，而非个人信念。

ex.en: During a separate observation, she saw that phones became a source of tension in the family.
ex.zh: 在另一项观察中，她发现手机已经成为导致家庭关系紧张的一个诱因。

ex.en: Close observation of the students' behaviour revealed that most of them learned better through practice than through lectures.
ex.zh: 对学生行为的细致观察表明，大多数人通过实践比通过听课学得更好。

ex.en: The astronomer's careful observation of the night sky led to the discovery of a new comet.
ex.zh: 这位天文学家对夜空的仔细观察促成了一颗新彗星的发现。

ex.en: The mountain-top observatory provides an ideal site for studying distant stars.
ex.zh: 这座山顶天文台为研究遥远的恒星提供了理想场所。

ex.en: Visitors can observe the night sky through the powerful telescopes at the observatory.
ex.zh: 游客可以通过天文台里高倍望远镜观测夜空。

ex.en: The old observatory still plays an important part in weather forecasting.
ex.zh: 这座老天文台仍在天气预报中发挥着重要作用。

senses: ②遵守，奉行(规则、法律、习俗等)
③(尤指就注意到或深思熟虑之事)说话，评论，评述
v. 看到，观察；遵守；评论
vt. 观察；注意到；评述；遵守（规则、法律等）
observe.usage: ob（表示“方向”）+serve（服务）→你要为我服务，你当然要朝着我的方向，观察我的行为，遵守我的要求→观察；遵守。；词根记忆：ob(表加强)+serv(服务)+e→观察到有人一直提供服务→观察；2024年阅读例：as Justice Brett Kavanaugh observed 正如大法官卡瓦诺所说；obser

ex.en: During a separate observation, she saw that phones became a source of tension in the family.
ex.zh: 在另一次观察中，她发现手机成了家庭关系紧张的来源。

ex.en: Weighing every other week allows me to observe and account for any significant weight changes.
ex.zh: 每隔一周称重一次，让我能够注意到体重的任何明显变化，并找到其原因。

ex.en: The scientist observed the behavior of the ants.
ex.zh: 科学家观察了蚂蚁的行为。

ex.en: Political observers expect the election results to be announced late on Friday night.
ex.zh: 政治观察家预计选举结果将在周五深夜公布。

ex.en: As a keen observer of village life, she recorded customs that outsiders rarely saw.
ex.zh: 作为乡村生活的敏锐观察者，她记录下了外人难得一见的习俗。

ex.en: International observers were invited to monitor the voting and count the ballots.
ex.zh: 国际观察员受邀监督投票并清点选票。

senses: vt. 使着迷；使念念不忘
obsess.usage: ob-（对着）+sess（坐）→整天坐在心头→萦绕于心→着迷。族obsession n.痴迷；萦绕；ob（加强）+sess（=sit坐）→坐在那儿一动不动，被迷住了

ex.en: In other words, if you're going to make a print product, make it for the people who are already obsessed with it.
ex.zh: 换句话说，如果你打算做纸质版，就专为那些醉心于纸质的人打造。

ex.en: Some students are so obsessed with grades that they ignore their health and friendships.
ex.zh: 一些学生对分数如此痴迷，以致忽视了健康和友谊。

ex.en: The fear of failure obsessed him throughout his otherwise brilliant career.
ex.zh: 在他本应辉煌的职业生涯中，对失败的恐惧始终萦绕心头。

ex.en: In other words, if you're going to print product, make it for the people who are already obsessed with it.
ex.zh: 换句话说，如果你要制作纸质印刷品，就为那些本就对此着迷的人制作。

ex.en: His obsession with cleanliness cost him hours of washing every single day.
ex.zh: 他对清洁的痴迷使他每天花数小时清洗。

ex.en: The media's obsession with celebrities has crowded out serious coverage of public policy.
ex.zh: 媒体对名人的痴迷挤占了严肃公共政策报道的空间。

ex.en: Turning a hobby into an unhealthy obsession can harm both work and family life.
ex.zh: 把爱好变成不健康的执念会损害工作和家庭生活。

ex.en: Fans' obsessive interest in celebrities has fuelled a growing paparazzi industry.
ex.zh: 粉丝对名人的痴迷关注催生了不断壮大的狗仔队行业。

ex.en: Rapid advances in software often render expensive hardware obsolete within a few years.
ex.zh: 软件的快速进步常常使昂贵的硬件在几年内就被淘汰。

phrases.p: put obstacles in the way of

obstacle.usage: 辨析:obstacle障碍(物);hindrance妨碍干扰;obstruction阻塞道路或通道；n.阻碍；障碍物；ob(逆)+stac(联想stand站)+le→站在对立面→障碍；词根记忆:ob(反)+sta(stand,站)+cle→反着站→障碍；索引p413

ex.en: But, when one considers the obstacles to achieving the meritocratic ideal, it does look as if a fairer world must be temporarily ordered.
ex.zh: 但是，在人们考虑到实现精英管理的诸多障碍时，看起来确实需要暂时建立一个更公平的世界。

ex.en: Lack of confidence is often the biggest obstacle to career progress for young employees.
ex.zh: 缺乏自信往往是年轻员工职业发展的最大障碍。

ex.en: High housing prices have become a major obstacle preventing young people from settling in big cities.
ex.zh: 高房价已成为阻碍年轻人在大城市安家的主要障碍。

senses: 阻隔,阻塞,遮断(道路、通道等)

phrases.p: obstruct the police in their duty

obstruct.usage: ob(反对)+struct(建造)→反对建造→妨碍；索引p413

ex.en: Fallen rocks obstructed the mountain road for several days.
ex.zh: 落石使山路阻塞了好几天。

ex.en: Critics accused the minister of trying to obstruct the official investigation.
ex.zh: 批评者指责这位部长企图阻挠官方调查。

ex.en: The tall new tower obstructs the view of the harbour from our windows.
ex.zh: 新建的高塔挡住了我们从窗口眺望海港的视线。

ex.en: Doctors warned that the obstruction of the artery could lead to a heart attack if left untreated.
ex.zh: 医生警告说，如果不及时治疗，动脉阻塞可能导致心脏病发作。

obtain.usage: v.得到，获得；ob（表示加强）+tain（拿）→一直想要拿到→获得，得到；索引p413

ex.en: Rested in the Pacific Ocean, Mauna Kea's peak rises above the bulk of our planet's dense atmosphere, where conditions allow telescopes to obtain images of unsurpassed clarity.
ex.zh: 莫纳克亚山位于太平洋，其山峰高耸于地球浓厚的大气层之上，那里的条件使得望远镜能获取无比清晰的像。

ex.en: I've been trying to obtain permission to publish this material.
ex.zh: 我一直在试图获得出版这份材料的许可。

ex.en: A refund is obtainable only if the ticket is returned within seven days.
ex.zh: 只有七天内退票才能获得退款。

senses: adj. 明显的，显而易见的；平淡无奇的，不必要的
obvious.usage: 辨析:obvious指极为明显，以至有目共睹；evident指根据事实成为显然的；apparent指一目了然或一想即通；adj.明显的，显然的；明确表 示的，毫不掩饰的；辨析：语气较强，指极为明显，有目共睹，无需说明和论证；索引p413

ex.en: It is obvious from the sales figures that the advertising campaign was a success.
ex.zh: 从销售数据可以明显看出，这次广告宣传活动是成功的。

ex.en: The answer seems obvious now, but at the time the problem puzzled even the experts.
ex.zh: 答案如今看来显而易见，但当时这个问题连专家也感到困惑。

ex.en: There is an obvious gap between what the report promises and what it actually delivers.
ex.zh: 报告所承诺的与实际交付的之间存在明显差距。

ex.en: Economists still debate why the crisis occurred in some countries but not others.
ex.zh: 经济学家仍在争论为什么危机发生在一些国家而在另一些国家没有发生。

senses: n. 场合；合适的机会；某次；……的时候；理由
occasion.usage: 发音类似我开心→开心是有时候的，分场合的→……的时候；场合；索引p413

ex.en: Only on rare occasions do I go out socially.
ex.zh: 只有在极少数情况下，我才会出去社交。

ex.en: The opening of the new bridge was a grand occasion attended by the mayor.
ex.zh: 新桥开通是一场有市长出席的盛大活动。

ex.en: On one memorable occasion, the entire class was invited to perform at the city theater.
ex.zh: 有一次令人难忘，全班受邀在城市剧院演出。

senses: adj. 偶尔的,间或发生的
adj. 偶然的，偶尔的；临时的
occasional.usage: occasion(时机)+al→时机(偶尔)的;派生occasionally adv.偶然地；拓展：on occasion(s) 偶尔，偶然，有时；索引p413

ex.en: He works for us on an occasional basis.
ex.zh: 他在我们这里做临时工。

ex.en: Apart from an occasional thunderstorm, the summer weather has been dry and pleasant.
ex.zh: 除了偶尔的雷阵雨，这个夏天的天气一直干燥宜人。

ex.en: Even occasional exercise is better for the heart than none at all.
ex.zh: 即便偶尔锻炼也比对心脏完全不运动要好。

ex.en: The museum occasionally opens its archives to the public for special exhibitions.
ex.zh: 这家博物馆偶尔向公众开放档案室举办特别展览。

senses: n. 职业；侵占，占领；消遣
occupation.usage: n.职业；消遣，业余活动；占 领；occupy 的派生词；索引p413

ex.en: A fifth grader gets a homework assignment to select his future career path from a list of occupations.
ex.zh: 一个五年级的学生拿到了一份家庭作业，从一份职业列表中选出自己未来的职业道路。

ex.en: A small but vocal group of Hawaiians and environmentalists have long viewed their presence as disrespect for sacred land and a painful reminder of the occupation of what was once a sovereign nation.
ex.zh: 长期以来，一个小规模但是敢于发声的夏威夷人和环保主义者团体一直将它们（指望远镜）的存在视为对神圣土地的不敬和曾经的主权国家遭到侵占的痛苦提醒。

ex.en: Please state your name, age and occupation on the application form.
ex.zh: 请在申请表上写明你的姓名、年龄和职业。

ex.en: Hearing loss is the most common occupational injury among factory workers.
ex.zh: 听力损失是工厂工人最常见的职业伤害。

senses: ③占领，侵占；④担任(职务)，居(某种地位)
v. 使用，占用；占领；使忙于；任职

ex.en: But just some 22,000 birds remain today, occupying about 16% of the species' historic range.
ex.zh: 但如今只剩下约22 000只鸟类，约占该物种历史数量的16%。

ex.en: Just 25 percent of the country's land is suitable for crop-growing, most of which is already occupied by arable fields.
ex.zh: 这个国家只有25%的土地适合种植农作物，而其中大部分已经被作为耕地占用。

ex.en: Preparing for the examination occupied most of his spare time last year.
ex.zh: 去年，备战考试占用了他大部分业余时间。

occur.usage: oc-(来)+cur(跑)→从暗处跑出来→出现；族occurrence，近happen；过去式、现在分词双写 r：occurred，occurring；v.(意外地)发生；存在，出现；词根:oc(to向)+cur(run奔跑)→由远到近跑向你→出现；例为2020年新题型；同根词根cur=to run奔跑；索引p413

ex.en: These pauses typically occur at about three per second, and the eyes then jump to another spot, until several important points in the image are registered like a series of snapshots.
ex.zh: 一般来说，这些停顿每秒发生三次，然后视线会移到另一个点上，直到图像上几个重要的点像一系列快照一样被记录下来。

ex.en: Most traffic accidents occur at intersections where drivers ignore the traffic signals.
ex.zh: 大多数交通事故发生在司机无视交通信号的十字路口。

ex.en: It suddenly occurred to her that she had left the documents on the train.
ex.zh: 她突然想起自己把文件落在火车上了。

senses: n. ①事件，事故，发生的事情(c)
occurrence.usage: 记：oc-（加强意义）+curr（发生）+-ence（名词后缀）→发生；辨析：occurrence 指偶然意外非预谋发生的事；accident 指伤亡事故、有前因可循；incident 指小事或政治性事件；n.发生的事，事件；发生， 出现；索引p413

ex.en: Power cuts were a common occurrence in the village before the new generator was installed.
ex.zh: 在新发电机安装之前，停电在村里是常有的事。

ex.en: The dictionary records the occurrence of each word in a wide range of modern texts.
ex.zh: 这部词典记录了每个词在大量现代文本中的出现情况。

ex.en: Flooding in this region is no longer a rare occurrence, according to the latest climate data.
ex.zh: 根据最新气候数据，该地区的洪灾已不再罕见。

ex.en: Scientists estimate that the ocean absorbs about a quarter of the carbon dioxide released by humans.
ex.zh: 科学家估计，海洋吸收了人类排放的约四分之一的二氧化碳。

oceania.usage: 附录Ⅱ 大洲名；形容词 Oceanian, Oceanic

ex.en: Oceania's isolated islands evolved plant and animal species found nowhere else.
ex.zh: 大洋洲孤立的岛屿演化出了其他地方没有的动植物物种。

ex.en: Oceanic currents move heat from the tropics towards the poles, moderating climates.
ex.zh: 洋流把热量从热带输向两极，起到调节气候的作用。

senses: adj. 海洋的,海洋中所有的

ex.en: Oceanic currents transfer heat from the tropics toward the poles, moderating the global climate.
ex.zh: 洋流把热量从热带输送到两极，从而缓和了全球气候。

ex.en: The train is due to arrive at six o'clock, giving passengers enough time for dinner.
ex.zh: 火车定于六点钟到达，乘客们有足够的时间吃晚饭。

ex.en: The breeding season for the deer begins in late September and peaks in October.
ex.zh: 鹿的繁殖季节从九月底开始，在十月达到高峰。

ex.en: The harvest festival, held every October, attracts visitors from across the region.
ex.zh: 每年十月举行的丰收节吸引着来自该地区各地的游客。

senses: 单只的,不成对的;临时的,不固定的;剩余的,多余的
adj. 奇怪的，古怪的；奇数的；大约
odd.usage: 同义strange,queer,unusual;extra,remaining,spare;反义even偶数的；adj.奇怪的；偶然出现的；奇数 的adv.（用于数字后）大约， 左右；拓展：odds n.可能性，概率；be at odds (with somebody) (over/on something)（就某事）

ex.en: But in my experience, using such methods to free up the odd 30 minutes doesn't work.
ex.zh: 但就我的经验来看，使用这样的方法挤出任意的30分钟时间来阅读并没有什么用。

ex.en: It seems odd that the company cancelled the project after investing so much money in it.
ex.zh: 该公司在投入那么多资金之后竟取消了项目，这看起来很奇怪。

ex.en: The numbers 1, 3 and 7 are all odd numbers.
ex.zh: 1、3 和 7 都是奇数。

ex.en: Even demographics are working against the middle class family, as the odds of having a weak elderly parent—and all the attendant need for physical and financial assistance—have jumped eightfold in just one generation.
ex.zh: 甚至连人口统计数据也对中产家庭不利，因为家庭中出现一个年老体衰的父亲或母亲——以及体力和经济上需要有人帮忙的所有这些护理需求——的几率在一代人的时间内猛增到了八倍。

ex.en: The odds of winning the lottery are so small that experts call it a tax on hope.
ex.zh: 中彩票的概率极小，专家称之为对希望的征税。

ex.en: Against all odds, the small team finished the project two weeks ahead of schedule.
ex.zh: 尽管困难重重，这个小团队还是提前两周完成了项目。

phrases.m: (在某人心目中)有良好/不良的声誉

ex.en: Residents complained about the unpleasant odour rising from the untreated sewage nearby.
ex.zh: 居民们抱怨附近未经处理的污水散发出难闻的气味。

senses: prep. 属于（某人或某物）的；……的一部分

ex.en: A large proportion of the students come from families of modest means.
ex.zh: 相当大比例的学生来自收入微薄的家庭。

senses: prep./ad./a. 离开；不在（某物）上面（的）

ex.en: The meeting was called off at the last minute because two key delegates fell ill.
ex.zh: 由于两位主要代表病倒，会议在最后一刻被取消。

senses: adj. 即兴的;未经准备的

ex.en: Politicians' off-the-cuff answers are often quoted more widely than their prepared speeches.
ex.zh: 政治家的即兴回答往往比他们的正式演讲被引用得更多。

senses: v. 冒犯，使不愉快；犯罪；犯法
offend.usage: 同义 displease，hurt，insult，disgust；反义 please；派生 offensive adj. 冒犯的，攻击的 n. 攻势；发音类似"恶犯的"→被恶意冒犯都会不高兴→冒犯，使不愉快

ex.en: They'll be offended if you don't go to their wedding.
ex.zh: 你若不参加他们的婚礼，他们会生气的。

ex.en: He apologized at once, fearing that his careless words might have offended her.
ex.zh: 他立刻道歉，担心自己随口的话可能冒犯了她。

ex.en: The new rules offend against the principle of fair competition.
ex.zh: 新规定违背了公平竞争的原则。

senses: n. 罪犯；妨害……的人（或事物）

ex.en: Repeat offender rates fell after the prison introduced vocational training schemes.
ex.zh: 监狱推出职业培训计划后，累犯率下降了。

senses: adj. 冒犯的,得罪人的,烦扰人的,使人恼怒的;攻击的

ex.en: The manager warned that offensive remarks about colleagues would not be tolerated.
ex.zh: 经理警告说，对同事出言冒犯是不会被容忍的。

ex.en: The army launched its offensive at dawn and quickly broke through the enemy lines.
ex.zh: 军队在黎明发动攻势，迅速突破了敌方防线。

ex.en: Some viewers found several jokes in the show deeply offensive.
ex.zh: 一些观众认为节目中的几个笑话极具冒犯性。

senses: v. 提供，提出；呈现，出现
vt. 提出；提供（东西或机会）；报价
offer.usage: render 的近义词。；词根记忆：of(toward,朝前)+fer(carry,携带)→带到前面→提出；索引p413

ex.en: For wild animals that cannot be returned to their natural habitats, zoos offer the best alternative.
ex.zh: 对于不能返回自然栖息地的野生动物，动物园提供了最好的选择。

ex.en: The company offered a generous salary to attract experienced engineers.
ex.zh: 该公司提供丰厚薪水以吸引有经验的工程师。

ex.en: She accepted the job offer without hesitation because it matched her career plans.
ex.zh: 她毫不犹豫地接受了这份工作邀约，因为它符合她的职业规划。

office.usage: 词组go to office去办公;out of office不执政,不当权;in office执政,当权

ex.en: She has held the office of chairman for three consecutive terms without serious opposition.
ex.zh: 她已连续三届担任主席一职，没有遇到有力的反对。

ex.en: The police officer explained the new traffic regulations to drivers gathered at the crossing.
ex.zh: 那名警官向聚集在路口的司机们解释新的交通法规。

senses: adj. 官方的,正式的,公务的

ex.en: Government officials refused to comment on the ongoing investigation.
ex.zh: 政府官员拒绝对正在进行的调查发表评论。

ex.en: A senior official confirmed that the two countries would resume trade talks next month.
ex.zh: 一位高级官员证实，两国将于下月恢复贸易谈判。

ex.en: English is the official language of the conference.
ex.zh: 英语是这次会议的官方语言。

ex.en: The retailer keeps detailed offline records because many customers still prefer paying in person.
ex.zh: 这家零售商保留详细的线下记录，因为许多顾客仍偏好在店内付款。

senses: v. 补偿，抵消(offsetting, offset, offset)
offset.usage: off（离）+set（放）→放到一边相抵→抵消。近义：compensate v. 补偿；off（离开）+set（放置）→放向另一边以平衡→抵消。近compensate v.补偿；索引p413

ex.en: The company plants trees to offset the carbon emissions produced by its factories.
ex.zh: 该公司植树以抵消其工厂产生的碳排放。

ex.en: Higher wages were offset by rising prices, so workers felt no real gain.
ex.zh: 上涨的物价抵消了工资的提高，因此工人们感觉没有实际收益。

ex.en: Gains in export sales were largely offset by the sharp rise in raw material costs.
ex.zh: 出口销售的增长在很大程度上被原材料成本的大幅上升所抵消。

senses: n. [C,U] 子女；后代；（动物的）崽
offspring.usage: off（出）+spring（春天出生的）→后代。单复数同形，不加s。同descendant n.后代

ex.en: His offspring are diligent and intelligent.
ex.zh: 他的后代既勤奋又聪明。

ex.en: Birds devote enormous energy to feeding their offspring during the breeding season.
ex.zh: 鸟类在繁殖季节投入巨大精力喂养后代。

ex.en: Many parents sacrifice their own comfort for the sake of their offspring.
ex.zh: 许多父母为了子女而牺牲自己的舒适。

senses: ad. 时常；常常；往往；大多

ex.en: Policy debates often ignore the people most affected by the decisions.
ex.zh: 政策辩论往往忽视最受这些决定影响的人群。

ex.en: Oftentimes the cheapest solution proves the most expensive once maintenance costs are counted.
ex.zh: 一旦算上维护成本，最便宜的方案往往被证明是最昂贵的。

ex.en: Small firms oftentimes lack the resources to comply with complex reporting rules.
ex.zh: 小公司往往缺乏遵守复杂报告规则所需的资源。

senses: v. 给……加润滑油,涂油,上油

ex.en: The price of oil rose sharply after the pipeline was damaged by the storm.
ex.zh: 输油管道被风暴损毁后，油价急剧上涨。

ex.en: The chemist recommended an antibiotic ointment for the cut on the child's arm.
ex.zh: 药剂师推荐了一种抗生素药膏来处理孩子手臂上的伤口。

ex.en: The inspector judged the temporary repairs okay until the bridge could be rebuilt.
ex.zh: 检查员认为临时修补在桥梁重建前是安全的。

ex.en: Tests confirmed the water was okay to drink, despite earlier fears of contamination.
ex.zh: 检测证实，尽管早先担心污染，这里的水仍可安全饮用。

ex.en: The price of oil fell sharply after several producing countries raised output.
ex.zh: 几个产油国提高产量后，油价大幅下跌。

senses: a. 老的；古老的；过去的

ex.en: The old belief that heavier objects fall faster was finally overturned by careful experiment.
ex.zh: 较重的物体下落更快的古老观念最终被严谨的实验推翻。

ex.en: Critics called the proposal old-fashioned, arguing that digital records would serve patients better.
ex.zh: 批评者称该提案陈旧过时，认为数字化记录会更好地服务患者。

ex.en: The cafe's deliberate old-fashionedness attracts tourists looking for a taste of the past.
ex.zh: 这家咖啡馆刻意营造的怀旧风格吸引着寻找旧日风味的游客。

ex.en: Many adolescents abandon sport when they move from primary to secondary school.
ex.zh: 许多青少年从小学升入中学后便放弃了体育运动。

ex.en: Olive groves have covered the hillsides of the Mediterranean for thousands of years.
ex.zh: 数千年来，橄榄树林一直覆盖着地中海的山坡。

ex.en: The omission of several key figures from the report raised doubts about its reliability.
ex.zh: 报告遗漏了几个关键数据，这使人们对其可靠性产生了怀疑。

senses: v. 省略；删除；忽略；遗漏
omit.usage: o（出）+mit（送）→往外送，送出去→省略，删去；遗漏，忽略

ex.en: Nothing healthful should be omitted in the diet.
ex.zh: 膳食中任何有益健康的东西都不应该被忽略。

ex.en: Important details were omitted from the final report, which led to serious misunderstanding.
ex.zh: 最终报告遗漏了重要细节，导致严重的误解。

ex.en: She omitted to mention that she had already accepted another offer.
ex.zh: 她没有提到自己已经接受了另一个邀请。

senses: n. 杂食动物;杂食的人

ex.en: As an omnivore, the bear feeds on berries, fish, and small mammals alike.
ex.zh: 作为杂食动物，熊既吃浆果，也吃鱼类和小型哺乳动物。

ex.en: The success of the project depends heavily on cooperation between the two departments.
ex.zh: 该项目的成败在很大程度上取决于两个部门之间的合作。

ex.en: Video games did not isolate the children; on the contrary, they formed new friendships.
ex.zh: 电子游戏并没有让孩子们孤立；恰恰相反，他们建立了新的友谊。

ex.en: Fast fashion keeps prices low by copying on-trend designs within weeks.
ex.zh: 快时尚通过在几周内复制流行设计来保持低价。

ex.en: Once the contract is signed, both parties are legally bound to honor its terms.
ex.zh: 合同一经签署，双方在法律上都有义务遵守其条款。

ex.en: The discovery of the oncogene opened a new path for targeted cancer therapies.
ex.zh: 致癌基因的发现为癌症靶向治疗开辟了新途径。

ex.en: No one explanation can account for the sudden collapse of the ancient civilization.
ex.zh: 没有哪一种解释能够说明这个古代文明突然消亡的原因。

ex.en: Critics warn that a one-shot payment will not solve a long-term funding crisis.
ex.zh: 批评者警告说，一次性拨款无法解决长期资金危机。

senses: a. 单向的；单行的；单程的；单方面的

ex.en: The bridge carries one-way traffic northwards during the morning rush hour.
ex.zh: 早高峰时段，这座桥只允许向北的单向通行。

ex.en: It is wise to ask oneself whether the evidence truly supports the conclusion.
ex.zh: 问问自己证据是否真正支持结论，这样做是明智的。

ex.en: The recipe requires a finely chopped onion fried slowly until golden brown.
ex.zh: 这道菜的做法要求把洋葱切碎，用慢火煎至金黄。

senses: adj. 联机的,在线的,联网的
online.usage: online services在线服务；online stores网店；索引p413

ex.en: More consumers now prefer online shopping because of its convenience and lower prices.
ex.zh: 如今更多消费者喜欢网上购物，因为它方便且价格更低。

ex.en: The university offers a range of online courses for students who cannot attend in person.
ex.zh: 这所大学为无法到场的学生提供了一系列在线课程。

ex.en: In recent years the newspaper has moved most of its content online.
ex.zh: 近年来，这家报纸已把大部分内容转移到了线上。

ex.en: The only effective way to curb pollution is to make polluters bear the full cost.
ex.zh: 遏制污染唯一有效的办法是让污染者承担全部代价。

senses: prep. 向，朝；朝向，面向（某个方向）

ex.en: The cat jumped onto the windowsill to watch the birds gathering in the garden.
ex.zh: 猫跳上窗台，注视着聚集在花园里的鸟儿。

senses: adj. 向前的,前进的;继续的
onward.usage: adv.向前；从……以后 adj.向前的，继续的；发展的， 进步的

ex.en: The expedition pressed onward despite the approaching storm and dwindling supplies.
ex.zh: 尽管风暴逼近、补给日益减少，探险队仍继续前进。

ex.en: Senior scientists opposed the decision to cut funding for long-term field research.
ex.zh: 资深科学家反对削减长期野外研究经费的决定。

senses: a. 不透明的；不透光的
opaque.usage: 反transparent a.透明的；clear a.易懂的。opaque既指物理不透明也指语义难懂

ex.en: The legal jargon in the contract is deliberately opaque, confusing ordinary consumers.
ex.zh: 合同中的法律术语故意晦涩难懂，使普通消费者感到困惑。
